title: Shock as safe Labor seat suddenly trends blue - so could this be a hint of what's to come at the federal election?
text:
By stream ward for AAP
Published: 03:43 GMT, February 9, 2025 | Updated: 03:43 GMT, February 9, 2025
The voting count was stopped until Monday after the dual partial elections in Victoria, with results too close to the call, but the first signs that show Werribee can no longer be a safe work seat.
Meanwhile, liberals have advanced in Prahran with 36.24 percent of the votes compared to 36.18 percent for the green candidate Angelica Di Camillo.
Political experts will seek the results of the clues about the electoral fortune of the Labor at the state and federal level, with a federal election that will be held in May.
The two Victorian surveys in Werribee in western Melbourne and Prahran inside the east of the city marked the first time that Prime Minister Jacinta Allan and the new opposition leader, Brad Battin, were tested in the bowling alley.
I work traditionally has Werribee, but the main vote of the party decreased 16.7 percent.
The resignation of former treasurer Tim Pallas triggered the partial election.
Early Sunday morning, liberal candidate Steve Murphy had 29.04 percent of the main votes, with John Lister de Labor at 28.71 percent.
Murphy (49.45 percent) was behind Mr. Lister (50.55) on a basis of two candidates.
The Minister of Finance, Katy Gallagher, said that while politicians watched the state partial elections, “nothing changed” for federal work.

Liberal leader Peter Dutton will expect the blue change in Werribee to be reflected in the next federal elections
“Our plans will continue to be the cost of living, providing help where we can, continue doing the things we need to do in Medicare and Infrastructure and work with state governments and territories,” he told ABC Insiders on Sunday.
“We will continue to sell that message and invest in those services.”
The liberals hoped to ensure an annoying victory in Werribee and also Bag Bag Prahran, a strength of the greens at stake after deputy Sam Hibbins renounced misfortune after the revelations that he had an adventure with a staff member.
Early Sunday morning, Liberal Rachel Westaway (51.6 percent) was ahead of Mrs. Di Camillo (48.4 percent) on a basis of two candidates.
Labor did not run in Prahran.
The result in Werribee’s partial choice in Victoria is still too close to call
The cost of living arose as the main concern for voters, along with the ability of housing.
Victorian liberals also campaigned a large extent about crime, with high profile murders and knife attacks in Prahran and Werribee attracting attention in recent months.
Mrs. Allan promoted the support measures of the living cost of her government and highlighted the divisions in the opposition after an December leadership spill.
About 104,000 people enrolled in the two electorates, with 28 percent of Prahran voters and 29 percent of those on Werribee tickets at the time or by post.
